criteria.idempotent_open: Authenticate the carrier and confirm nonce freshness, then let delivery_id alone drive the outcome: done replays done, dead replays dead, unknown ids get 404, failed deliveries remain pending with a recorded attempt. Lease ownership is not consulted. Safety comes from downstream delivery_id deduplication and a state machine with no path back from delivered.
criteria.ownership_checked: Admit an ack only from the worker currently holding the lease, proven by matching worker_id and version, otherwise 409 lease_lost. Acknowledgements from stale holders or after expiry must reclaim before reporting. Stronger attribution, more conflict arms and more companion reclaim paths.

ack.instructions: For acknowledgement, is authenticating the carrier plus idempotent delivery-id handling enough, or must the acking worker prove live lease ownership?

criteria.multi_batch: Claim up to K rows in a single transactional round trip using a recursive loop, applying identical lease/version handling per row. Saves round trips but forces recursion inside the transaction decision, with mock coverage per level and a wider decision surface to assert.
criteria.single_page: Claim at most one row per call: pick the oldest claimable row with a lookup-first read, then a version-guarded conditional write. The Can reads straight-line and asserts mechanically; the companion iterates to empty and retries honestly on race losses. Batch shape stays companion-side.

claim.instructions: Is per-request multi-row claiming worth its complexity, or should claims stay single-row with companion-side paging?

criteria.bearer_nonce: Authenticate with the shared secret as a bearer header, plus timestamp freshness and a single-use nonce. Minimal Can logic and no per-message signature. Nonce storage still stops in-window replays, yet altered bodies are not cryptographically detected, so the design depends on loopback/trusted scope and deployment transport security.
criteria.body_fields: Embed timestamp_ms and nonce in every carrier JSON body and sign the exact bytes with HMAC-SHA-256; headers transport only the protocol version and the hex tag. Mirrors the already-proven provider check, avoids canonical-string construction, binds every field to the tag, and rejects replays through the unique nonce insert.
criteria.header_canonical: Place timestamp, nonce and signature in headers, signing an assembled canonical form of timestamp, nonce, method, path and body. Route and payload are both covered, while Can must assemble the canonical form and parse the extra headers. The nonce table still absorbs replays.

envelope.instructions: Which authentication envelope for carrier calls fits best under the fixed guarantees and language limits?

state.constraints: Available Can machinery: HMAC-SHA-256 across exact bytes as already proven for provider deliveries, bounded JSON bodies, integer math with ordering, text::join for canonical forms, integer JSON timestamps beside a wall clock, transactional conditional UPDATE with affected-row counts, and a unique-nonce table. Descriptors allow SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with no RETURNING. One-row decisions stay straight-line; several rows per decision demand recursion plus per-level mocks. Equality comparison is exact, not constant-time, and that limit stays documented.
state.criteria: Select the leanest design that resolves R16-03, holds at-least-once delivery with idempotent ack under two contending workers, recovers from supervisor restart through idempotency alone, asserts cleanly, and surfaces versioned honest failures using C-E statuses.
state.decided: The settled P09-B3 shape is: lease-table claims through a portable lookup-first claim_outbox(worker_id, lease_until) transaction, never a locking read; protocol version carries worker identity, lease expiry and heartbeat; at-least-once delivery with idempotent ack and C-C unknown-write wording; past N versioned attempts the companion flags the row via dead_letter while Can keeps the dead-letter table and decide_ack dead-letter rules; a restarted companion under its supervisor simply redelivers whatever is unacked. Loopback with trusted-carrier scope stays per F-R11-04. Zero outside users, zero compatibility baggage, environment-only secrets.
state.goal: Deliver F05, the authenticated webhook pair between Can and its companion: the Can program keeps ledger, outbox, attempts, idempotent decide/ack transactions and commit-unknown reconciliation, while the companion takes claims, delivery, retry timing, bounded parallelism, poison handling, crash recovery and destination policy. The R16-03 gap closes by authenticating carrier endpoints so unauthenticated, replayed or malformed carrier traffic is rejected.
state.threats: Assume adversaries replay sniffed carrier calls, mutate bodies on the wire, and race claims with a rogue second worker. Concurrent lease takes must settle with no duplicated business effect; any doubled downstream send is caught by delivery_id deduplication rather than by pretending delivery happens once. Secrets live only in environment snapshots, never in logs, and each response honors C-E status honesty (200/400/401/404/409/413/503 with bodies).
